text:
Maria (infra): seeing a spike of GPU ECC errors in us-west2 on fleet-gpu-prod, node g-node-17 crashed with kernel oops. Can we triage?
Dan: on it. Do we have telemetry? which model traffic affected?
Priya: noticing increased 5xx from runtime on route /v1/generate in us-west2, latency up ~40%. Looks like a handful of nodes degraded.
kube-bot: Incident created: INC-20260318-4873 — GPU node crash + ECC errors — assigned to infra-oncall.
Ryan (oncall): I'm pulling node logs now. Maria, can you confirm which node IDs are impacted?
Maria (infra): g-node-17, g-node-21, g-node-22 show ECC corrected/unrecoverable patterns. g-node-17 is down, others flapping.
Dan: start draining g-node-17 and g-node-21. Use the GPU-aware drain to preserve pods: `kubectl drain g-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector=gpupod=true`
Priya: Also update routing weight on us-west2 pool to shift 25% to us-west1 and 20% to eu-west until we stabilize.
Tom: Scheduled the route shift. prod-router: set weight up to us-west1: +25%, eu-west: +20% via rollout policy. Watch for QoS.
Maria (infra): I've kicked the drains. Logs show repeated "ECC Uncorrectable" followed by GPU reset attempts.
Dan: paste of dmesg: ```[ 12345.6789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, CE error, pid 3210, GPU 0, reason: ECC Uncorrectable
[ 12345.6790] kernel: GPU hung, resetting...```
Priya: Noted. Could be a failing DIMM on the board or GPU memory wear. HW-Ops, can you validate on-prem replacement availability?
HW-Ops: We have replacement GPUs in staging rack but need approval to hot-swap. Propose draining entire host and RMA card. ETA 4-6 hours if replacement arrives.
Ryan (oncall): For immediate capacity, let's enable burst capacity in dedicated pool and spin up 6 transient instances in us-west1 with same GPU profile. Also bump autoscaler min for the rotor pool +3.
Tom: Doing transient spin-up. Also watching cost — this will add ~$2.1k/hr if sustained. Flagging finance for cost watch.
Maria (infra): Creating ticket for vendor escalation with logs and timestamps. Also tagging any models pinned to older quantization variants — Priya, can you check fallbacks? We may need to fallback to cpu-safe route for critical customers.
Priya: Will check pinned versions. For high-SLA customers, we should move them to dedicated capacity in another region temporarily.
Dan: After draining, I see pods rescheduled successfully except two that failed due to node-specific docker-layer caches. Manual eviction fixed it.
kube-bot: Node g-node-17 status: NotReady -> SchedulingDisabled (drained) at 1719804560
Maria (infra): Running vendor diag: nvidia-smi -q output showing ECC errors incrementing and GPU resetting frequency >10 per hour. I'll attach logs to the RMA ticket.
HW-Ops: Confirmed RMA request opened with vendor case #VND-9932. They requested core dumps, nv-hostengine logs, and PCI IDs. Sending via secure upload.
Ryan (oncall): Traffic shift in effect. Latency in us-west2 decreased but overall capacity is down ~18%. Keep monitoring for backpressure on batches.
Tom: Autoscaler +3 applied and transient instances up. Observability shows queue length stabilized but token cost for transients starting to tick.
Maria (infra): Post-mortem/notes: action items — replace GPU on g-node-17, run stress test on replacement, add automated eviction on repeated ECC >3 within 1h, update runbook with vendor RMA steps, and add alert for ECC Uncorrectable Xid 79.
Priya: I'll create a prompt-set regression test to ensure model outputs unchanged after moving traffic. Also add customers to the incident notification list.
Dan: Next steps for ops: schedule maintenance window to swap cards, label nodes with hw-age metadata, and consider gradual fleet refresh if ECCs appear on >2% of GPUs in region.
Maria (infra): Good work. Keep updates here. If vendor confirms systemic batch failure we'll escalate to leadership. :thumbsup:
